mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SL 280 or SL 350 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M104 engine for the SL 280 costs £2,200-£3,200 supply-only; a rebuilt M272 engine for the SL 350 costs £2,800-£4,500 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - V6 work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M272 balance shaft failure on a Mercedes SL 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start lasting a few seconds is the classic warning sign on the M272 V6 engine. If ignored, it can lead to catastrophic engine failure. M272 engines with engine numbers below 2729..30 468933 require updated balance shaft parts per Mercedes TSB.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SL 280 or SL 350 petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M104, M112, M272 and M276 engines are all fundamentally refined and durable, but each has well-documented weaknesses. The M104's biodegradable wiring harness affects 1993-1995 models, while the M272's balance shaft wear is a known catastrophic failure. With these addressed, all are capable of 150,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SL 280 and SL 350 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M104, M112, M272 and M276 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Balance shaft issues on the M272 typically appear between 60,000-90,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SL 280 or SL 350 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SL is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M104 costs £2,200-£3,200 - far less than replacing a £5,000-£15,000 classic. The SL 350's higher value (£6,000-£30,000) makes replacement even more justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes SL 280 or SL 350 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M104 requires approximately 6.5 litres; the M112/M272/M276 V6s require approximately 7.5-8.0 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SL 280/350 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SL 280 and SL 350 have represented the entry-level and mid-range petrol options across three generations of Mercedes' iconic roadster. The SL 280 debuted in the R129 generation in 1992 with the M104 2.8-litre inline-six, offering 193hp of smooth, refined power. The SL 350 arrived with the R230 generation in 2001, powered by the M112 3.7-litre V6 producing 245hp - later replaced by the M272 3.5-litre V6 in 2004 with 268hp, and finally the M276 3.5-litre V6 in the R231 generation with 306hp. These engines represent the accessible yet refined heart of the SL range.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz SL 280/350 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The SL 280's M104 inline-six and the SL 350's M112, M272 and M276 V6s are among Mercedes' most refined petrol engines, but each has well-documented weaknesses that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The M104 is notorious for biodegradable wiring harness failure, while the M272 suffers from balance shaft idler gear wear. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M104 Biodegradable Wiring Harness Failure - The Classic SL 280's Electrical Nemesis
problems.rootCause: Mercedes used a biodegradable insulation material on wiring harnesses from 1993-1995. Over time, the insulation breaks down, causing short circuits, misfires, rough running and, in severe cases, no-start conditions. This is the single most common electrical issue on early R129 SL models. One owner reported replacing the wiring harness on their 1994 280SL to resolve persistent running issues.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 1992-1997 SL 280 is worth approximately £5,000-£15,000 depending on condition and mileage. These classic roadsters are appreciating assets for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a justifiable investment for preservation-minded owners.
problems.recommendation: If your SL 280 experiences intermittent running issues, misfires or warning lights, have the wiring harness inspected immediately. problems.group: M272 Balance Shaft Idler Gear Wear
problems.h4: M272 Balance Shaft Idler Gear Wear - The SL 350's Most Notorious Failure
problems.rootCause: Early M272 V6 engines used a balance shaft idler gear with insufficient surface hardening, causing premature wear. This throws metallic debris through the oil galleries, jamming the timing chain tensioner and starving cam phasers of lubrication. Rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign. M272 engines with engine numbers below 2729..30 468933 require updated balance shaft parts per Mercedes TSB. One R230 SL350 owner reported that "the rattling on startup is a sure sign".

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: STAR diagnostic, cam/crank correlation check, borescope inspection
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether balance shaft is worn

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace balance shaft with updated hardened gear, timing chain, tensioner, guides
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before debris has damaged bearings

repairOptions.longevity: If debris has circulated through oil galleries

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2004-2011 SL 350 is worth approximately £6,000-£18,000 depending on mileage and condition. The R230 SL 350 retains strong values for well-maintained examples, making replacement a justifiable investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise on cold start from your SL 350, act immediately. The M272's balance shaft wear is a known catastrophic failure. Specialist balance shaft replacement at £2,400-£3,600 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the engine has been run with metallic debris circulating, a full rebuilt M272 engine is the only safe option.

problems.h4: M112 Harmonic Balancer Failure - The Early SL 350's Age-Related Issue
problems.rootCause: The M112's harmonic balancer (crankshaft pulley) has a bonded rubber layer that deteriorates with age, heat cycling, and exposure to oil. This can cause the outer ring to separate at speed, potentially leading to catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Visual inspection of harmonic balancer for cracks or rubber deterioration

problems.h4: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - The R231 SL 350's Cold-Start Rattle
problems.rootCause: The M276's hydraulic secondary chain tensioners can lose oil pressure over time, causing a metallic rattling noise on cold starts. The tensioners have a weak spring and rely on oil pressure to maintain tension. Mercedes issued TSB LI05.10-P-056435 covering updated tensioners and check valves.
